## Purpose

This procedure describes the operation, image capture, and maintenance
of the Echo Labs Revolve microscope. The Revolve is a hybrid instrument
that combines an upright microscope (for prepared glass slides) and an
inverted microscope (for live samples in dishes) in a single rotating
platform, with an iPad retina display replacing the traditional
eyepiece [@echolabs_revolve; @murphy2012]. The microscope supports bright field, phase contrast,
fluorescence, and dark field imaging modes. It represents a substantial
investment by the EA Program and requires careful handling.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All use of the Echo Labs Revolve microscope in the
  EA Program laboratory, including bright field, phase contrast,
  fluorescence, and dark field modes in both upright and inverted
  configurations
- **Does not apply to:** Electron microscopy, confocal microscopy,
  dissecting/stereo microscopes, or other optical microscopes not
  described here
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133

## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, authorize instrument access    |
| Lab Manager       | Schedule maintenance, manage software updates, maintain optics |
| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report malfunctions        |
| New Students      | Complete training (including video modules) before independent use |

## Definitions

- **Brightfield illumination:** Standard transmitted-light microscopy in which the sample is illuminated from below and absorbing or scattering structures appear dark against a bright background; the most common mode for stained biological specimens.
- **Darkfield illumination:** A transmitted-light mode in which the direct beam is blocked; only obliquely scattered light reaches the objective, making unstained transparent structures appear bright against a dark background.
- **Epifluorescence:** A fluorescence microscopy mode in which excitation light is directed through the objective onto the sample, and the emitted fluorescence is collected back through the same objective; enables fluorescent stain visualization.
- **Eyepiece (ocular):** The lens assembly through which the observer views the magnified image; typically 10x; total magnification equals eyepiece magnification times objective magnification.
- **Fluorescence filter cube:** An interchangeable optical block containing an excitation filter, dichroic mirror, and emission filter matched to a specific fluorophore (e.g., DAPI, FITC, TRITC).
- **Numerical aperture (NA):** A dimensionless number characterizing the angular range of light an objective can accept; higher NA provides better resolution and light-gathering; the resolving power is approximately $d = 0.61\lambda / NA$.
- **Objective:** The primary lens closest to the specimen; available in magnifications of 4x, 10x, 20x, 40x, and 100x (oil immersion); higher magnification objectives have shorter working distances.
- **Working distance:** The distance between the front lens of the objective and the coverslip when the specimen is in focus; decreases with increasing magnification; critical for thick samples.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Optical:** The fluorescence LED produces intense illumination.
  Avoid looking directly into the excitation light source. The iPad
  display eliminates the need to view through an eyepiece, reducing
  direct optical exposure, but reflected excitation light can still
  cause eye strain.
- **Electrical:** Keep liquids away from the iPad and the microscope
  base. If immersion oil or sample fluid contacts the electronics,
  disconnect power immediately and notify the lab manager.
- **Physical:** The microscope is heavy. Use both hands when rotating
  the platform between upright and inverted modes. Objective lenses and
  condensers are precision optics; handle with care.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses (especially during fluorescence mode)
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves (when handling biological specimens or immersion
  oil)

### Emergency Procedures

If a biological spill occurs on or near the microscope, clean and
disinfect per [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd).
If immersion oil contacts the iPad or electronics, power off
immediately and contact the lab manager before attempting cleanup.

## Procedure

### Microscopy Modes Overview

The Revolve supports four imaging modes. Select the mode appropriate
for the specimen and analysis:

| Mode            | Best For                                   | Staining Required? |
|:----------------|:-------------------------------------------|:-------------------|
| Bright field    | Stained specimens, gross morphology        | Recommended        |
| Phase contrast  | Unstained transparent specimens, live cells | No                |
| Fluorescence    | Specimens with fluorescent labels or autofluorescent pigments (e.g., cyanobacteria) | Fluorophore-dependent |
| Dark field      | Fine structures, edges, unstained specimens | No                |

### Starting the Microscope

1. Press the power button on the top left corner of the iPad [@echolabs_revolve].
2. Swipe to unlock. The overhead microscope light should turn on and a
   live image should appear on the screen.
3. If the light does not turn on or no image appears, open the
   **Echo Labs** app from the home screen
4. If the screen reads "Light Off," tap **BF** at the top of the screen
   to enable bright field illumination
5. Load the prepared slide into the stage clips (upright mode) or place
   the culture dish on the stage (inverted mode)

### Rotating Between Upright and Inverted Mode

::: {.callout-important}
This is the most mechanically delicate operation on the Revolve. Follow
each step carefully to avoid damaging the objectives or condenser.
:::

1. Rotate the nosepiece to move all objective lenses out of the optical
   path
2. Unscrew the stage and carefully lift it away from the microscope
   body without contacting the condenser
3. Push the iPad flat so it is out of the rotation path
4. Press the release button on the upper back of the microscope body
5. Rotate the microscope body 180 degrees counterclockwise until it
   clicks into place
6. Reinstall the stage and tighten the mounting knob until secure
7. Rotate the desired objective lens back into position and realign the
   iPad

### Using Bright Field Mode

1. Confirm that **BF** is selected on the screen
2. Place the slide or specimen on the stage
3. Start with the lowest magnification objective (4x) to locate the
   region of interest
4. Use the outer coarse focus knob (to the right of the iPad) to bring
   the specimen into approximate focus, then use the inner fine focus
   knob to sharpen the image
5. Use the stage translation knobs to move the slide: the lower knob
   moves the stage left/right, the upper knob moves it toward/away from
   you
6. Increase magnification by rotating the nosepiece to the next
   objective (10x, 40x)
7. Adjust brightness, contrast, and color balance using the sliding
   controls on the bottom right of the screen. Adjust the physical
   light intensity using the flat knob on the bottom right of the
   microscope body.

### Using Phase Contrast Mode

Phase contrast converts differences in refractive index into
differences in brightness, allowing transparent, unstained specimens to
be visualized.

1. Set up the specimen in bright field mode first and bring it into
   focus
2. Select the phase contrast ring that matches the current objective:

| Objective | Phase Ring |
|:----------|:-----------|
| 4x        | PhL        |
| 10x       | Ph1        |
| 40x       | Ph2        |
| 100x      | Ph3        |

3. Tap the **PH** mode selector on the screen (if available) or
   manually rotate the condenser turret to the matching phase ring
4. Fine-tune focus and centering as needed

::: {.callout-note}
Phase contrast images may exhibit a bright "halo" around large objects
(positive phase contrast) or a dark edge (negative phase contrast).
This is a normal optical artifact caused by diffracted light passing
through the phase ring. A "shade-off" effect, in which homogeneous
regions appear at the same intensity as the background, is also
expected.
:::

### Using Fluorescence Mode

1. Tap **FL** at the top of the screen to switch to fluorescence mode
2. The fluorescence LED will illuminate automatically
3. Place the specimen on the stage and focus using the same procedure
   as bright field
4. Minimize illumination time to reduce photobleaching. Locate the
   region of interest in bright field first, then switch to fluorescence
   only for image capture.

::: {.callout-warning}
Fluorophores lose their ability to fluoresce over time when illuminated
(photobleaching). Work quickly, minimize unnecessary excitation, and
consider using photoprotective mounting media when possible.
:::

### Using Dark Field Mode

until this section is completed.*

### Capturing and Exporting Images

1. To capture an image, tap the white camera shutter button on the left
   side of the screen
2. Enable the **anti-shake** feature (hand icon below the shutter
   button; it should turn orange when active) to reduce vibration blur
3. To review captured images, tap the gallery icon (square) at the top
   left of the screen. Tap **Done** to return to the live view.
4. Export images via a flash drive connected to the iPad, AirDrop, or
   the cloud sharing option in the Echo Labs app
5. Use a consistent file-naming convention:
   `YYYY-MM-DD_SampleID_Objective_Mode.jpg`

### Using Oil Immersion (100x Objective)

1. Focus the specimen at 40x first
2. Rotate the nosepiece to an empty position (no objective in the light
   path)
3. Place a single small drop of immersion oil directly on the cover
   slip at the point of illumination
4. Rotate the 100x objective into position. The lens front element
   should contact the oil without trapping an air bubble.
5. Focus carefully using the fine focus knob only
6. After use, immediately clean the 100x objective with lens cleaning
   solution and lint-free tissue. Never allow oil to dry on the lens.
7. Clean the slide or dispose of it as appropriate

### Replacing the Condenser

The Revolve has two condensers: one for low magnification (4x through
60x) and one for 100x oil immersion. Condenser swaps require care
to avoid contaminating or scratching the optics. Consult the lab
manager before performing this procedure for the first time.

*Detailed replacement steps TBD; to be documented with the lab manager.*

### Shutdown and Daily Maintenance

1. Remove the specimen from the stage
2. Rotate the nosepiece to the lowest-magnification objective (4x) or
   to an empty position
3. If oil immersion was used, clean the 100x objective immediately
4. Wipe any sample residue or oil from the stage with a Kimwipe
   dampened with lens cleaning solution
5. Close the Echo Labs app on the iPad
6. Press and hold the power button to turn off the iPad
7. Cover the microscope with the dust cover


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### Optics Cleaning

If specks or smudges appear in captured images that do not move when
the specimen is translated, the optical path may need cleaning:

1. Do not attempt to clean internal optics without the lab manager
   present
2. For objective lens surfaces, apply a small amount of lens cleaning
   solution to lint-free tissue and gently wipe in a circular motion
   from center to edge
3. For dust on internal surfaces, remove the arm and use short bursts
   of compressed gas duster. Do not allow the compressed air canister
   to become cold, as it will deposit a film on the optics.
4. For persistent contamination, contact Echo Labs support or the lab
   manager

### Image Quality Checklist

Before accepting an image for publication or analysis, verify:

- Focus is sharp across the region of interest
- Illumination is even (no hot spots or vignetting)
- Scale bar or magnification metadata is recorded
- Anti-shake was enabled during capture
- In fluorescence mode, confirm that photobleaching has not
  significantly degraded the signal


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Used immersion oil tissues    | Standard trash                           |
| Used microscope slides (non-hazardous) | Broken-glass box if glass; standard trash if plastic |
| Biological specimen waste     | Biohazard bag if applicable; autoclave before disposal |
| Spent lens cleaning solution  | Standard trash (small volumes on tissues) |

## Training Record

Before using the Revolve microscope independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Watch the Echo Labs training video at
   <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IcubmIsxa7w>
4. Observe a trained operator demonstrate upright/inverted rotation,
   all four imaging modes, and oil immersion setup and cleanup
5. Demonstrate proper startup, focusing, image capture, and shutdown
   under supervision
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Microscope Anatomy Quick Reference {.appendix}

| Component               | Function                                    |
|:-------------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| iPad display (eyepiece replacement) | High-resolution live view and image capture |
| Arm                      | Connects optics to base; removable for optical path cleaning |
| Stage                    | Flat platform for specimens; translatable via X/Y knobs |
| Nosepiece (turret)       | Holds and rotates objective lenses          |
| Objective lenses         | 4x, 10x, 40x, 100x (oil); determine magnification |
| Condenser                | Focuses illumination light onto the specimen |
| Coarse/fine focus knobs  | Outer knob = coarse focus; inner knob = fine focus |
| Light intensity knob     | Physical control on the base for illumination brightness |
| Phase contrast turret    | PhL, Ph1, Ph2, Ph3 rings matched to objectives |
| Fluorescence LED         | Excitation source for fluorescence imaging  |
| Platform release button  | On the upper back; allows 180-degree rotation between upright and inverted modes |
